title: How should Ziva write the lunch money for five days?
description: Ziva pays the same price for lunch on each of five school days. Two ways of writing the money for the week are told side by side, and the video stops on a question about them.
teaching_notes: One idea: the same money can be written in more than one way. Ask each child to say whether the two ways mean the same, and what to call such a sentence. Do not confirm either answer; watch for children who say the shorter way must give a different amount.

source: Lunch money for five school days
video_script.why: Before the words expression and value, the child meets two ways of writing one total and has to say what they are.
video_script.substitution: Picture the five days as five equal payments written in a row, and the same payments written in a shorter way.
video_script.anchor: Ziva's lunch money for five school days, written in two ways

names.Ziva: the child who pays for lunch at the school canteen

never_show: the total of the five days
an equals sign between the two ways of writing
maths_rules: Ziva pays 25 rupees on each of five school days, Monday to Friday.
One way writes 25 five times with plus signs between; the other writes 5 times 25. Neither is called an expression and no total is shown.
The open question: do the two ways say the same thing, and what are such sentences called.
video_script.design: One idea: one amount of money, two ways to write it. Assumes nothing. No wrong idea is broken. The photo sits as a backdrop in the first beat and fades before the plates arrive; the two ways are shown in words only, with no sign on screen.
